text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Unlisted construction and engineering group Koop buys Germany's Maerkische Ingenieurbau and Ingenieurbau Altmark. (p1)
- Gerrit Ypma of D66 political party sees a great future for staff share option schemes. (p4)
- Dutch companies are still confused after last week's revelation that European Court's 'Securitel verdict' could mean many Dutch rules and regulations are not legally valid. (p5)
- Small and medium-sized businesses association MKB sees no cost saving from cleaner production. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Parliament criticises Economics Minister Hans Wijers for keeping potential consequences of 'Securitel verdict' secret.
- New disease 'para-TBC' threatens cattle. (p1)
- Costs of launching new euro currency will be recovered in two year's time according to Dutch central bank. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Schiphol airport backs plans to develop new airport on land reclaimed from the sea. (p1)
- Cost of damage caused by severe storms at the weekend runs to tens of millions of guilders. (p3)
- Brewer Heineken has taken steps to ensure it can enter the Indian market as soon as opportunities arise. (p23)
TROUW
- Christian Democrats (CDA) criticise transport minister Annemarie Jorritsma for mismanagement of subsidies to state-owned Netherlands Rail (NS). (p4)
- Unions and employers in the engineering sector fail to reach agreement on early retirement scheme. (p8)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Container transhipment firm Bell Line may close its Rotterdam operations. (p12)
